affected_system: fixed-route public transit service and passenger connections
alternatives: advance high-risk work within verified feasible windows for route timetable, recovery, and connection schedule
use rolling risk and capacity updates to reschedule route timetable, recovery, and connection schedule
pair multi-route timetable optimization with stochastic travel times with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Trips, stops, vehicle observations, disruptions, and calendars share a versioned service day.
Passenger loads and transfer behavior are measured or represented as bounded assumptions.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
baseline: continue the fixed operating calendar for route timetable, recovery, and connection schedule.

constraints.description: The transit reliability and passenger continuity schedule must respect declared labor, access, sequencing, notice, and completion windows.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
decision_owner: transit chief operating officer and service-planning director
decision_question: How should trips and recovery time be scheduled to balance reliability, transfers, and operator rules?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The transit reliability and passenger continuity schedule must respect declared labor, access, sequencing, notice, and completion windows.
independence_key.decision_object: route timetable, recovery, and connection schedule
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for route timetable, recovery, and connection schedule passes documented checks for effective dates, time zones, calendars, lead times, completion semantics, and update cadence.
independence_key.intervention_mechanism: multi-route timetable optimization with stochastic travel times
independence_key.primary_outcome: passenger-weighted excess wait and missed-connection time

intended_claim: A versioned schedule design for comparing declared alternatives affecting route timetable, recovery, and connection schedule, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: passenger-weighted excess wait and missed-connection time
distributional gap in passenger-weighted excess wait and missed-connection time
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not call an optimized timetable published, staffed, or operated.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for route timetable, recovery, and connection schedule passes documented checks for effective dates, time zones, calendars, lead times, completion semantics, and update cadence.

title: Schedule headways, recovery time, and timed connections
transportability_risks: Fare policy, headways, fleet, labor rules, topology, and passenger behavior vary by operator.
Reliability metrics may not transfer between schedule-based and frequency-based service.
